title: Spin-Orbit-Torque-Driven Recurrent Motion of Synthetic Antiferromagnetic Skyrmions for Magnetic Clocking
authors: Sayan Mathur, Payal Bhattacharjee, Saswati Barman, Anjan Barman
abstract: Magnetic skyrmions in synthetic antiferromagnets have emerged as attractive information carriers for spintronic technologies due to their compensated topology, which mitigates the skyrmion Hall effect and facilitates reliable current-driven transport. Here we present a frequency-tunable magnetic clocking concept based on the recurring translational motion of SAF skyrmions and define the material conditions needed to realize it in a Pt/Co/Ru/Pt/Co multilayer. Using micromagnetic simulations, we investigate the combined effects of interfacial Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction and interlayer Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida exchange coupling, delineating the parameter space in which coupled Néel-type skyrmions with opposite topological charges form a stable, topologically compensated pair. Under spin-orbit torque excitation, the SAF skyrmions exhibit resilient longitudinal transport with minimal transverse deflection using periodic boundary conditions. Periodic boundary conditions serve as an idealized model for closed-loop racetrack geometries, facilitating the study of continuous transport cycles and long-range steady-state dynamics. The oscillation frequency is readily modified by the applied current density and material characteristics, offering a pathway to field-free nanoscale timing components. Moreover, the threshold-activated initiation of recurrent transport mimics tonic-spiking behavior, indicating possible use in neuromorphic signal generation. This work establishes SAF skyrmions as versatile building elements for future spintronic functional devices by integrating topological protection, controllable transport, and cyclic dynamics.
summary: This work proposes using synthetic antiferromagnetic (SAF) skyrmions in multilayered magnetic systems to create a highly efficient, field-free nanoscale clock. By utilizing the SAF structure, the detrimental Skyrmion Hall Effect is suppressed, allowing SOT to drive stable, recurrent translational motion. This demonstrates a versatile platform for next-generation spintronic functional devices.
main_problem: The paper aims to develop a frequency-tunable, field-free magnetic clocking concept using the recurring translational motion of synthetic antiferromagnetic (SAF) skyrmions.
main_result: SAF skyrmions exhibit stable, continuous, and recurrent longitudinal transport when driven by Spin-Orbit Torque (SOT), enabling nanoscale timing components with high energy efficiency.
method: The study employs micromagnetic simulations and analytical derivations based on the Thiele equation to model the coupled dynamics of the skyrmion pair.
model_or_system: The physical system is a Pt/Co/Ru/Pt/Co multilayer containing SAF skyrmions. The dynamics are governed by the LLG equation and simplified using the Thiele equation, exploiting the cancellation of the net gyrovector due to opposite topological charges.
key_observables: Resilient longitudinal transport, oscillation frequency (tunable), energy per cycle ($\approx 0.53 	ext{ fJ}$), and the elimination of the Skyrmion Hall Effect.
important_parameters: Interfacial Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (iDMI), interlayer RKKY coupling ($\sigma_{	ext{RKKY}}$), and applied current density (for tuning frequency).
main_assumptions: The skyrmion is treated as a rigid object for dynamics, and periodic boundary conditions are used to model closed-loop racetrack geometries.
figures_summary: Not specified (Notes only contain theoretical derivations and parameter discussions, not figure descriptions).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the physical necessity of SAFs to mitigate the Skyrmion Hall Effect, deriving the energy functional and radius, and finally applying the Thiele equation to predict stable, recurrent, and tunable clocking dynamics.
why_interesting: While focused on spintronics, the concept of using topological protection and controlled, cyclic dynamics (like spiking behavior) for information processing shares conceptual parallels with engineered quantum state evolution or controlled dissipation in open quantum systems.
